newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VICENZA THE FIAT TO JUVENTUS' FERRARI.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VICENZA THE FIAT TO JUVENTUS' FERRARI.

text.p: A British pop song was once released with the memorable if cumbersome title of "All I want for Christmas is a Dukla Prague away strip."
The tune went down moderately well with lovers of the bizarre but would torment Vicenza fans.
Dukla are the only foreign team that the 95-year-old north-eastern Italian club has ever met in a major European competition and that was in the 1978/79 UEFA Cup.

The Czechs came to Vicenza and left 2-1 winners on aggregate, pushing the Italians -- who missed a penalty and hit the goalpost -- back to the wilderness and leaving just the memory of that musically infamous away strip.
In the same 95 years since Vicenza was founded, the club has never won a league or cup honour of any description.

It is against that backdrop of occasionally heroic failure -- but generally just failure -- that Saturday's Italian league match between the dominant European champions and serie A leaders Juventus and humble Vicenza takes place.
This season has seen a revival of hope at Vicenza unseen since the gloom that descended in 1978 when the small provincial club embarked on 17 years in lower divisions.

If Vicenza win at Turin's delle Alpi stadium, they will be another huge step closer to returning to Europe next season after having also reached the Italian Cup final on Tuesday night for the first time in their history.
They will also pull off a considerable upset, despite having already beaten Juventus 2-1 once this season.
There can hardly be two teams in the top flight of serie A more separated by their own history -- the one all-achieving and the other forever on the outside looking in.
Juventus have the money, the fans, an enormous publicly-owned stadium that they would love to be rid of and a list of greats stretching back over a century.
Vicenza have just two overwhelming past stars -- which they share with Juventus but claim proudly among their own.
Paolo Rossi and Roberto Baggio, the Italian heroes of the 1982 and 1994 World Cups, were both discovered by humble Vicenza only to move on and achieve greatness in Turin.
Juventus, holders of a record 23 league titles in their 100 year history and of every other trophy that can be won by a club, turned both men into domestic champions.
Massimo Briaschi, whose goal against Dukla makes him the only Vicenza player ever to score in Europe, also went to Juventus and won the league title there.
Rossi in fact started off at Juventus in 1972 but was loaned to Como in 1975 before his serie A debut when a knee injury convinced Juventus he would not make the grade.

He then joined Vicenza, a small northeastern town near Venice famous for its Renaissance architectural delights, and helped the serie B club into serie A in 1977 where it then gave Juventus a fight for the title and finished runners-up.
"Pablito" ended the season as top scorer with 24 goals while his stylish team, purveyors of some of the most attractive football seen in Italy, were dubbed "Real Vicenza".
That was Vicenza's best ever placing and it was a flash in the pan. The following season they were relegated.
Rossi, banned for two years for involvement in an illegal betting scandal, moved on to Juventus and became the hero and top scorer of Italy's 1982 World Cup triumph.
While Vicenza were down in serie C1 in 1982, local boy Roberto Baggio emerged on the scene.
In the 1984-85 season he scored 12 goals in 29 appearances and then headed for Fiorentina and serie A. Vicenza, cash-strapped and struggling, could never have kept him.
Fiorentina, wealthier but still provincial, also found it hard and in 1990 Baggio went to Juventus.
But just occasionally, as in 1977 and earlier this season, the two clubs have found themselves talked of in the same breath among the elite list of potential Italian champions.

In November last year, the inexpensive Vicenza side went alone at the top of the league for the first time in their history and gave newspapers ample space to fulminate about other club's costly mistakes in signing big name foreigners.
Vicenza have just two full first team overseas stars -- the classy Uruguayans Marcelo Otero and Gustavo Mendez. They also have 17-year-old Cameroonian Pier Wome.

Juventus have a line up full of them -- including Croat Alen Boksic, Frenchmen Zinedine Zidane and Didier Deschamps, Uruguayan Paolo Montero and Montenegrin Vladimir Jugovic -- although several will be absent on Saturday.

The revelation of the first half of the season, with a handful of stalwarts who had served the club all the way up from serie C joined by low-price youth signings, Vicenza forced themselves into the reckoning for the honours.
It has gone awry since then, with the club sliding back down and with only one point in their last three matches.
"Vicenza is no more," declared the Turin daily Tuttosport on Monday after they drew 1-1 with Piacenza.
Juventus, five points clear at the top of the table and now 10 ahead of seventh-placed Vicenza, will hope that is true although the cup run clearly points otherwise.
But the provincial team are still ahead of champions Milan, and big guns Fiorentina, Lazio and Roma.
The title is a dream, but a UEFA Cup or Cup Winners' Cup place -- and a chance to finally lay the ghost of Dukla Prague -- still beckons for the team of journeymen heroes.
